intent: Establish a symmetric five-sensor baseline with a wide, forward-mounted sensor array and a mid-sized, moderately heavy body. I am keeping this geometry unchanged for the first race so that the Integrator can measure a clean baseline. Expected result: the robot completes most development tracks with few line-loss events. Under consideration, not committed: a narrower array (about 0.03 m total span) if the controller oscillates on tight bends, and a longer forward offset if the robot reacts late.
learning: Initial geometry is a prior, not yet tested. Sensor span versus tape width, and forward offset versus steering lag, are the two hypotheses to test first.
rationale: This is iteration 0, so there is no Integrator feedback or race telemetry yet. I am choosing a conservative baseline from the contract's physical logic. Five sensors spaced 0.02 m apart across x = -0.04 to +0.04 cover 0.08 m, about three times the 0.025 m tape width, so the line stays inside the array through moderate offsets and bends. Sensors sit 0.03 m ahead of the axle so they read the line before the wheels reach it, which leaves time for the controller to respond. A 12 mm footprint is about half the tape width, giving a clear on-line versus off-line reading without too much blur on bends. The track width is 0.12 m, a mid-range value that balances turning agility against stability at speed. Wheel radius is 0.03 m, giving a reasonable ground speed for the 1.5 m/s average needed to finish in 3 s. Body width 0.12 m gives an off-track limit of about 0.0425 m, which is looser than the 0.06 m floor and tolerates some error before the run ends. Mass is 0.8 kg, and the body is 0.18 m long. I expect a completable run with low line-loss events. Sensor spacing and forward offset are the main levers I expect to revisit once the Integrator reports how the sensor array behaves in the controller.
